_comment: Trust policy for liftoff-github-deploy -- the role GitHub Actions assumes.
OIDC rather than stored access keys: GitHub presents a short-lived signed token,
AWS verifies it, and no long-lived credential ever exists in a repo secret. A
leaked secret is then not a standing compromise.
Requires a one-time IAM OIDC identity provider for
⚠️ The `sub` condition is the security boundary, and getting it wrong is the
classic mistake. Written as below it permits ONLY workflows running on the main
branch of this one repo. If it were `repo:chrrstiang/liftoff-app:*`, then any
pull request -- including one opened from a fork -- could assume this role and
push images to your ECR. Do not loosen it to a bare wildcard.
To also allow tag-triggered deploys, add
as an additional entry rather than widening the existing one.
